sources.citation: Hewitt, B. G. (1995). Georgian: A Structural Reference Grammar. London Oriental and African Language Library 2. Amsterdam and Philadelphia: John Benjamins. doi:10.1075/loall.2
sources.used_for: Standard descriptive grammar in English: sound system, declension, verb classes and screeve formation, syntax. Its table of contents is the one the syllabus was checked against.
sources.access: In copyright. The publisher's preview (front matter, contents, abbreviations, alphabet, chapters 1-2 and chapter 3 up to about p. 53: phonemes, phonotactics, stress, noun declension, syncope, numerals) was opened and read on 2026-11-12. Chapter 4 (verbal morphology) and chapter 5 (syntax) were not opened.

sources.citation: Aronson, H. I. (1990). Georgian: A Reading Grammar. Corrected edition (first published 1982; third printing 1991 with addenda). Columbus, Ohio: Slavica.
sources.used_for: Main teaching grammar: lesson order (present series and nominative/dative first, then the aorist and ergative, then series III), the four conjugations, pronunciation description, reading passages.
sources.access: Open PDF hosted by the Slavic and East European Language Resource Center (SEELRC, Duke/UNC). Front matter, contents, introduction and Lesson 1 (phonology, alphabet) opened 2026-11-12 (pp. 1-30 of 538). Later lessons not yet opened; verifiers should open the relevant lesson before citing it. The direct curl connection to port 8080 failed; the file was read through the Firecrawl scraper.

sources.citation: Hewitt, G. (2005). Georgian: A Learner's Grammar. 2nd ed. (1st ed. 1996). London and New York: Routledge.
sources.used_for: Second teaching grammar; lesson-by-lesson presentation of verb classes, version and series III; dialogues in colloquial register.
sources.access: In copyright; not consulted. Copies found online were unauthorised and were not opened.

sources.citation: Wiktionary, the free dictionary (English edition): Georgian entries, declension tables and conjugation tables; Wiktionary:Georgian transliteration and Module:Geor-translit.
sources.used_for: Checking individual forms: full noun declensions (all nouns tested had tables) and full conjugation tables for many verbs (e.g. დაწერს, ხატავს, თამაშობს, მიდის, არის, ხედავს, აკეთებს, ჭამს, სვამს, ცხოვრობს, მოდის, აშენებს). Also the transliteration scheme this guide uses.
sources.access: Open (CC BY-SA). Query with python3 tools/wikt.py <word> Georgian. Many verbs, including most indirect (inversion) verbs such as უყვარს, აქვს, ჰყავს, უნდა, have entries but no conjugation table: check those elsewhere.

sources.citation: Lingua.ge. Conjugation of Georgian Verbs (online conjugator, about 700 verbs).
sources.used_for: Second check for conjugations Wiktionary lacks (inversion verbs, irregular verbs, imperatives). The site states it is still correcting errors: treat a form found only here as needing a second source.
sources.access: Open online; index page opened 2026-11-12 (through the Firecrawl scraper; direct curl returned 406). Individual verb pages not yet opened.

sources.citation: Dryer, M. S. and Haspelmath, M., eds. (2013). The World Atlas of Language Structures Online. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. Language: Georgian (wals_code_geo).
sources.used_for: Typology values opened 2026-11-12: 1A consonant inventory moderately large; 2A vowel quality average (5-6); 4A voicing in plosives and fricatives; 7A ejectives only; 13A no tones; 49A 6-7 cases; 81A SOV; 85A postpositions; 87A adjective-noun; 98A case marking of full NPs active-inactive (with glossed examples); 100A verbal person marking accusative; 102A both A and P marked on the verb.
sources.access: Open.
